messages:
maya: Heads-up — we're planning to onboard fjord-edge-8b for an internal edge runtime benchmark. Want a quick compliance check on packaging/redistribution rules for quantized weights (q4/q8).
nate: Do we know the upstream license? repo has a LICENSE but it's not one of the usual ones.
alex: Link: https://hf.co/fjord-edge-8b/blob/main/LICENSE (short snippet pasted)
legal: can you paste the exact license text? if it's a custom grant we'll need to read the clauses.
maya: pasted the relevant clause: 'Redistribution of model binaries is permitted only with explicit attribution and when distributed in source form; redistribution of compiled or transformed weights (including quantized formats) requires prior written permission.'
legal: Ok — that's a clear restriction. TL;DR: we can host & serve via our inference layer for customers, but we cannot re-publish the quantized binaries or include them inside public containers without written permission from the copyright holder.
maya: So packaging a docker image with the q4 weights baked in is a no-go unless we get permission, right?
legal: Correct. Bundling the quantized weights in a public container or uploading to a public registry = redistribution. Even obfuscating or changing the format doesn't avoid restriction; conversion to a new numeric format is considered a derivative work in this license.
alex: What about distributing a container that pulls the weights at runtime from a private S3 bucket we control (access-limited)?
legal: That's safer — private hosting with access controls and no public mirrors is allowed for internal use or enterprise customers under our agreements. But watch customer contracts: if a customer requires redistributing the runtime bundle to their internal infra, they may also be redistributing the weights, so we'd need permission or an alternate flow.
sara: From an ops perspective, we can implement a serve-only package: container image contains only the model loader + code, and runtime fetches weights into ephemeral storage. That avoids shipping binaries in the image.
maya: Good. Also: any requirements for attribution/notice in the UI or API docs when we serve the model?
legal: The clause requires attribution when redistributing. For hosted serving, we should include provenance in the model card and internal inventory: origin URL, license text, and a visible 'model_card.provenance' entry. For customer-facing docs, add a short attribution line and a link to the license. Not strictly required to show on every API response, but keep it in the console and onboarding docs.
nate: What about quantization experiments for our internal evals? e.g., we want to run q4->q8 conversions and ship results to bench results repo.
legal: Internal experiments and derived metrics are fine. Just ensure derived artifacts (quantized files) are not committed to public repos. If you want to publish a benchmark paper or blog that includes model weights or a download link to quantized weights, you must get written permission.
maya: Ok. Action items: 1) change packaging to fetch-at-runtime pattern, 2) add model_card provenance and license link, 3) tag model in registry as 'license: restricted' and 'serve_policy: private_or_hosted_only', 4) legal will request written permission if we need redistribution.
legal: We'll draft an email template to request permission from the model authors if you want to pursue redistribution. Note that some authors permit redistribution for academic/research only — check for additional clauses.
devops-bot: CI: model-registry entry created: fjord-edge-8b (license=restricted, serve_policy=private_or_hosted_only) :white_check_mark:
maya: Thanks everyone. One more: QA — when we run quantized vs fp16 evals, should we run a focused regression test set to catch safety/behavioral diffs?
sara: Yes — run the standard eval suite + the new prompt-safety and hallucination checks. If any regression > 3% on our golden prompts, flag for review before release.
maya: Perfect. I'll update the onboarding checklist and cc legal for permission template follow-up. :thumbsup:
